Priya — quick update from infra: we saw a transient surge in queued requests targeting the embeddings pool in us-west-2 starting 08:42. Autoscaler scaled but a subset of hosts experienced degraded network I/O while the scale completed (kernel-level NIC flaps on 4 hosts). We're isolating those instances off the pool now.

Taking actions:
- Isolating affected hosts (in progress)
- Forcing a gentle drain then replacement to reduce queued latency on the pool (in progress)
- Sending logs (we'll attach condensed logs)

ETA for restored steady-state: 30-45 minutes barring additional flaps. I'll keep this thread updated every 15 min.

-Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-resolution update and next steps (Embeddings latency, Jan 22)

Julia — thanks again for your patience today. Quick post-resolution summary:

Timeline (high level):
- 08:42 PST — First customer reports; elevated queue depth observed in us-west-2 embeddings pool
- 08:46 PST — Autoscaler initiated; NIC-level I/O errors detected on 4 hosts
- 08:50 PST — SREs isolated affected hosts and started replacement/evacuation
- 09:18 PST — Steady-state restored for the pool; 95th percentile latency returned to normal ranges

Impact:
- Two Acme nightly jobs failed (we confirmed the timestamps you shared); search pipeline experienced elevated 95th latency for ~35 minutes
- Root cause (preliminary): NIC firmware-induced I/O flaps on a small subset of hosts during a high-concurrency window; not related to request content or model correctness

Immediate remediation completed:
- Affected hosts removed and replaced; autoscaler tuned to reduce aggressive queuing in rare burst scenarios
- KV cache warming adjustments to reduce cold-start latency for large batched embeddings requests

Next steps / actions for Redwood (committed):
- Complete full postmortem with timeline and remediation plan within 72 hours (link to draft: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B_postmortem_drive_link)
- Provide a redlined customer-facing summary for your internal stakeholders (we’ve attached a template)
- Review firmware/update policy across our embeddings fleet to prevent recurrence

Compensation & credits: we will run a scope analysis as part of the postmortem. If we confirm measurable impact beyond our SLA, we will issue pro-rated credits and discuss any additional remediation.

Attachments: condensed logs we collected, postmortem-draft-v1.md, customer-comm-template.docx

If you want immediate mitigation for production search, you can also toggle to the fallback embedding route we discussed previously; Ben, can you confirm the toggle instructions for Acme?

Thanks — I’ll follow up once the postmortem is finalized.

-Priya
